newsitem.title: POLAND: EARLY ZLOTY RANGE-BOUND IN QUIET TRADE, SEEN FLAT.
newsitem.headline: EARLY ZLOTY RANGE-BOUND IN QUIET TRADE, SEEN FLAT.

text.p: The zloty fluctuated against the basket of currencies in early trade follownig world dollar/mark changes with no clear local sentimet to give it direction, and is likely to drift mostly sideways today, dealers said.
They said the local unit may swing by some 0.1 point toward and away from the parity rate but expected no major changes on the shallow and slow market ahead of the long weekend.
"In a nutshell, one should expect range trading between minus 0.7 and 0.9 percent weaker than parity today," said Mateusz Bieniek, forex dealer at Societe Generale in Warsaw.

At 0830 GMT the zloty was 0.88/0.94 percent weaker then its currency basket against minus 0.73/0.88 percent at opening. It was at 3.4805/20 to the dollar and 1.8965/80 to the mark against opening's 3.4770/20 and 1.8925/55 respectively.

Dealers said the market lost its speculative edge from earlier this week as news of the central bank's intention to tighten its monetary policy grew old and foreign players stayed on the sidelines. "Banks are less willing to speculate as they are understaffed due to holiday season, they become active only when large foreign orders come, which is now unlikely," said Marek Cherubin, forex dealer at Bank Creditanstalt SA.

On the money market early one-day rates fell by more than one percentage point but soon rallied to 21.50/22.50 percent for O/N and 22.99/23.40 percent for T/N against opening's 22.70/22.95 and 23.00/23.25 respectively.
Dealers said rates may fall again as the expected central bank's drainage might not be large enough to satisfy the overliquid market ahead of the long weekend.
Dealers expected the central bank to stage a 14-day reverse repo and 91-day NBP-bill sales today at unchanged maximum rates. -- Tomasz Oljasz +48 22 653 9700
